text:
deploy-bot: ALERT: High rate of CUDA OOMs observed on decode-pool-3 in us-west-2. 172 failures in 2m. Paging oncall.

alice (oncall): seeing lots of `cuda error: out of memory` in decoder logs, nodes flapping. Streaming requests getting killed mid-response, customers report dropped responses. Attaching sample log: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z decoder[pid=421]: cuda: out of memory at decode_step.cpp:312
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z decoder[pid=421]: trace id=tx-9a3e client=acct-42 token_count=47200
```
This looks like runaway generation; token_count seems super high.

ben (eng-runtime): on it. Early hypothesis: some clients are passing a bad `max_tokens` (or server-side cap got removed in the last rollout). Telemetry shows a spike from a single customer IP doing long-running chat sessions.

carla (sre): oncall handover in 10m. Alice, can you confirm if this is confined to decode streaming path vs batch endpoints? Need blast radius.

alice (oncall): only decode-streaming nodes in decode-pool-3 and decode-pool-5 so far. Batch endpoints unaffected. P95 latency spiked from 120ms to 3.2s; error-rate 502/503 up 6%.

sam (support): I'm fielding customer messages. One enterprise customer (acct-42) saw ~40% of requests dropped in the last 15m. Drafting a short note to send to their CSM once we have cause.

ben (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation plan: 
1) enforce an ingress hard cap for `max_output_tokens` at the gateway (set to 8k) so a runaway header can't push decoder into OOM.
2) apply a temporary routing rule to divert traffic from decode-pool-3 to decode-fallback-small (quantized) where possible.
3) scale down affected replicas to force new nodes with patched env.
I'll push the hotpatch now.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered: `scale deployment decode-stream --replicas=0 --namespace=inference` by alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): doing controlled cordon/drain on decode-pool-3 nodes to avoid more OOM churn. Using: 
```
kubectl -n inference cordon node/worker-uw2-13
kubectl -n inference drain node/worker-uw2-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

carla (sre): paging secondary oncall ben. Ben, please take over if you can apply the gateway cap quickly. I'm staying to monitor and customer comms.

ben (eng-runtime): pushed gateway patch: `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192` enforced in ingress-plugin v1.4. Command: 
```
helm upgrade ingress-plugin ./charts/ingress -n infra --set maxOutputTokens=8192
```
Patch applied, verifying...

deploy-bot: deploy ingress-plugin v1.4 completed in 17s.

alice (oncall): after cap applied, we still see some OOMs but rate dropped 85%. Streaming errors falling back to 1-2 per minute. Good. Redirecting traffic now.

ben (eng-runtime): activated routing fallback: set `route.group=low-memory-variant` for accounts with >10 concurrent streaming sessions. This moves long sessions to quantized model paths automatically.

sam (support): sent interim note to affected CSMs: "We've detected a spike in long-running streaming sessions causing GPU OOMs. We've implemented a temporary cap and routing fallback; service degradations are reduced. We'll follow up with root cause and a timeline for permanent fix." :white_check_mark:

julia (product): which customers were most affected? Do we need to notify legal/enterprise support?

alice (oncall): initial list: acct-42 (enterprise), acct-181 (mid-market sandbox), and ~120 random API keys with high token churn. acct-42 had highest error rate. Sam, please prep targeted outreach for acct-42 and one-sentence notice for the rest.

ben (eng-runtime): root cause data: in 1.17.3 rollout last night we changed `default_max_output_tokens` behavior to inherit client-specified `max_tokens` when present. A regression allowed unbounded client values to bypass our internal guard for streaming paths. A customer-side test client sent `max_tokens: 1000000` and then resumed streaming, generating extremely long outputs until OOM.

carla (sre): noted. That explains the single-IP spike. We'll record in incident timeline. Is there any data loss for customer prompts?

alice (oncall): requests that hit OOM were dropped; however we have request/response logs so can replay for debugging. Customer payloads are in logs for acct-42. No PII observed in the sample logs we checked but will coordinate with privacy team.

ben (eng-runtime): permanent fixes planned: 
- Revert the risky inheritance behavior (hotfix commit queued).
- Add gateway validation to always clamp `max_tokens` for streaming to safe range.
- Add server-side per-stream token budget enforcement and early termination w/ clear error to client.
- Add e2e test that simulates client with extremely large `max_tokens`.
I'll open PRs and attach to this thread.

alice (oncall): executing controlled restart of decode-stream fleet with patched env var to ensure new pods pick up clamped behavior. ETA 12m.

deploy-bot: restart deployment decode-stream -n inference triggered by alice (oncall).

carla (sre): monitoring dashboards: error rate back to 0.8% and request drops down. CPU/GPU memory stabilized. Marking incident as "mitigated" but not resolved.

sam (support): acct-42 CSM confirmed receipt; they'll collect logs on their side and asked for a postmortem. I'll loop them in when we have the RCA.

julia (product): please add a blurb to status.redwood.com: short explanation + ETA for full fix. Use non-technical wording.

alice (oncall): incident notes for postmortem: 
- Trigger: client-specified `max_tokens=1000000` after rollout changed inheritance behavior.
- Impact: GPU OOMs on decode streaming pools, request drops, higher latency for streaming customers; acct-42 saw ~40% dropped responses for 18m.
- Mitigation: gateway cap at 8192, routing fallback to quantized pool, cordon/drain of flapping nodes, restart of decode-stream pods.
- Actions: revert behavior, server-side token budgets, e2e tests, alert tuning for token churn.

carla (sre): assigning action items: 
- ben: PRs for revert + guards (priority P0).
- alice: postmortem write-up and timeline (P0).
- sam: customer comms + CSM follow-ups (P1).
- ops: run retro on node drain procedure to reduce churn.

ben (eng-runtime): opened PR #3741 for revert and #3742 for per-stream budget enforcement. Linking in thread.

alice (oncall): thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket and change channel state to "monitoring". If errors climb again, page back. :eyes:

deploy-bot: incident state changed: ACKNOWLEDGED -> MITIGATED by alice (oncall).

carla (sre): closing loop: please add test vectors to the CI that include `max_tokens: 1000000` and a streaming harness to validate early termination.

sam (support): will schedule a 1:1 with acct-42 CSM tomorrow.

julia (product): once RCA done, we should surface learnings in runbook and maybe add a small UX guard in our SDKs to warn users about insane `max_tokens`.

alice (oncall): end of thread — monitoring.
